coordinates.locator: Meyrin Site – Point 1 (CERN and its Neighbours)
coordinates.note: No CERN geodetic-survey or metrology publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the underground ATLAS cavern was found (checked 2026-09-17: CERN survey and metrology conference papers, the ATLAS JINST detector paper, CERN's neighbours and open-days pages for Point 1). The numeric value comes from an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for the surface enclosure named 'CERN - Point 1 (ATLAS)'. That geocoder source is listed with the record's sources for provenance but is not cited on this coordinate. The precision was widened from 300 to 500 m because this is an unsurveyed estimate.

depth.note: Rock overburden above the ATLAS cavern; home.cern states the same figure ('It sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site').
depth.quote: ATLAS has the dimensions of a cylinder, 46m long, 25m in diameter, and sits in a cavern 100m below ground.

depth_rock.quote: sits in a cavern 100m below ground

name: LHC Point 1 (ATLAS)
notes: No official CERN or geodetic publication giving WGS84 coordinates for LHC Point 1 was found (checked 2026-09-17; cds.cern.ch is behind bot protection, and home.cern and atlas.cern state only that ATLAS 'sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site, close to the village of Meyrin'). The coordinate value is a geocoder estimate; see the coordinate note.

summary.plain: The underground cavern at the edge of CERN's Meyrin campus where the ATLAS detector sits, about 100 metres below ground. It is one of the eight access points around the 27-kilometre Large Hadron Collider ring and the place where two of the LHC's proton beams are made to collide inside ATLAS.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 1 on the CERN Meyrin site: the UX15 experimental cavern ~100 m below the surface housing the ATLAS detector, together with its surface buildings and the ATLAS control room.
